hook: New chemical probes tag sulfur radicals on proteins inside living bacteria, pinpointing the exact residues.
summary: Protein radicals are short-lived and have been hard to find across a whole cell. The authors built thioacetylene probes that bind covalently to cysteine radicals and used mass spectrometry to locate the labeled sites in live E. coli, including a known site in ribonucleotide reductase. The probes also tagged some glycyl radical sites, and the work was done only in one bacterium.
title: Mechanism-Guided Development of Thioacetylene Probes for Chemoproteomic Profiling of Cellular Protein Thiyl Radicals
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
